policy_question: How should growth-related infrastructure costs be allocated and disclosed so decision-makers can assess impacts on housing delivery, affordability, councils, existing ratepayers, developers and future residents?

run_metadata.notes: Fill one record per arm. Keep inputs, prompts and outputs identical in scope where feasible.

known_facts: The Ministry says the government intends to replace development contributions with a development levies system as part of Going for Housing Growth.
The proposed levies concern water supply, wastewater, stormwater, transport, reserves and community infrastructure, with separate levies for each service.
The proposed charge basis is expected growth and the aggregate forecast cost of infrastructure capacity across defined levy areas.

The Ministry page records 56 submissions to the 2025-26 consultation from councils, developers, industry groups, Māori housing organisations and individuals. It reports councils were strongly supportive of replacement while developer views were mixed.
The consultation's 56 submissions are not a representative public opinion poll and cannot by themselves establish national public consensus.

The Ministry says the Local Government (Infrastructure Funding) Amendment Bill is being prepared for introduction in the first quarter of 2027; further input is anticipated through the select committee process and later methodology/disclosure consultation.
not_established_by_the_supplied_sources: Whether the proposed system will lower or raise house prices or rents.
Whether a levy is passed through to buyers, renters, landowners, developers, taxpayers or ratepayers, and in what proportions.
Whether projected infrastructure demand or development will match actual outcomes.
Whether people across New Zealand support the policy; the submission set is not representative of the population.
Whether the Anon Politician workflow improves policy-analysis quality.
